messages:
Sophie: Quick follow-up to the compact-policy RFC I posted last week — I sketched a narrow implementation plan for a compact trie + tag-layer encoding that the runtime can hot-swap. Posting because I want feedback on operational tradeoffs.
Dmitri: curious — what's the primary win? memory or lookup CPU?
Sophie: both. idea is to compress common predicate chains into a dense trie so route match is O(length) with small memory working set. gains on our microshards where tenant rules are repetitive.
Kevin: sounds promising. downside? harder to explain routing decisions to customers or SREs.
Sophie: yep. big tradeoff: compact encoding loses obvious per-rule IDs. plan is to surface explainability hooks that map trie nodes back to rule fingerprints. That adds a 1-2ms attribution step.
Maria: how does this affect hot-reload safety? we had races with the old policy-hotload.
Sophie: proposal includes an immutable snapshot descriptor + versioned pointer swap. runtime applies compactor off-thread, validates with sim harness, then atomically swaps descriptor. rollback every swap is supported.
Ben: what about telemetry? we need per-rule counters for billing and regressions. Compacting might collapse counters.
Sophie: we keep a lightweight indirection: node -> canonical-rule-fingerprint(s). counters keep using fingerprints. compactor guarantees stable fingerprint IDs for semantically identical rules.
Dmitri: can we avoid walking the fingerprint map on every request? that's extra overhead.
Sophie: the common path will have direct node->route pointer. explainability/fallback path does the fingerprint expansion only when a debug flag is on or on trace-sampled requests.
RuntimeBot: sim-run finished: compactor v0.1 produced 3.8x reduction in policy table memory and 12% p95 lookup CPU reduction across sampled tenant traces. 14/1000 mismatches in edge-case predicates (investigating).
Maria: 14 mismatches is worrying. any pattern?
RuntimeBot: mismatches concentrated in regex-ish predicates and tenant overrides with negations. compactor currently normalizes simple predicates only.
Kevin: ok, so we need a compatibility shim: fallback to full evaluator when predicate normalization fails. That keeps safety while enabling compact path for the rest.
Sophie: agreed. implementation checklist I propose: 1) compactor service (offline but nearline) 2) atomic descriptor swap + rollback API 3) node->route fast path + optional explainability expansion 4) compatibility shim to full evaluator for un-normalized predicates 5) sim harness + canary rollout plan 6) telemetry mapping to fingerprints.
Dmitri: rollout plan thoughts? start with low-traffic tenants, enable sim-check-only for the rest?
Sophie: exactly. three phases: sim-only (generate reports), passive route (use compact path but verify results against full evaluator), active route with canary (5% traffic), then ramp.
Ben: add a metric: 'compact.path.mismatch_rate' and alert if > 0.05% during passives.
Maria: ops playbook? who is oncall for rollback during canary?
Sophie: runtime-oncall + me. descriptor rollback API is single-button in console + automated health-check that flips if mismatch_rate spikes or error-rate increases.
Dmitri: performance tests needed for explainability hook. if 1-2ms attribution hits p99 overall we must optimize.
Sophie: will add microbenchmarks and a perf budget in the RFC addendum.
Kevin: one more thought: we should keep a human-readable audit dump for every compact descriptor for compliance.
Sophie: yes — compact descriptor -> expanded audit JSON stored in blobstore (immutable). small cost but required.
RuntimeBot: note: sim harness flagged a tenant with heavy negative predicates; recommendation: exclude that tenant from passive route until compactor supports negations.
Sophie: thanks, RuntimeBot. action items: Sophie to land compactor prototype branch; Dmitri/Kevin to design explainability API; Maria to draft rollback playbook; Ben to wire telemetry/alerts. I'll schedule a check-in next Wed. :thumbsup:
